A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PIXEL-M4 research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and all 19 figures and seven tables can be matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, dependency parsing, NER, data-efficiency, probing, and representation-analysis results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds CANINE-S evaluations across the three main downstream tasks.

M1.justification: PIXEL-M4 retains the same four-language pretraining, bigram rendering, masked autoencoder architecture, reconstruction objective, and downstream prediction procedure. No proposed method component changes.

E1.justification: The pretraining languages, downstream datasets and languages, low-resource scenarios, LINSPECTOR tasks, and retrieval coverage are unchanged. CANINE-S is evaluated on the existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds CANINE-S throughout classification, parsing, and NER comparisons in Tables 1–3, retaining PIXEL-BIGRAMS and all monolingual BERT comparators. This introduces a multilingual character-level comparator across the entire main evaluation suite, substantially broadening the comparison beyond monolingually pretrained models.

E3.justification: Existing splits, metrics, training budgets, hyperparameters, and testing procedures are unchanged. Appendix A.2 explicitly assigns CANINE-S the same experimental setup and hyperparameters as the pixel models.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.3 retain the same data-efficiency experiments, layerwise linguistic probes, t-SNE analysis, and cross-lingual retrieval analysis. Their plotted evidence is unchanged; no new ablation or robustness analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight random-seed repetitions for constructing the data-efficiency subsets and averaging the five runs with the highest validation performance for pixel-model test results. Uncertainty displays and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 add substantive comparative findings: CANINE-S averages 63.7 classification F1, 73.9 parsing LAS, and 76.8 NER F1, versus PIXEL-M4's 58.7, 79.3, and 76.6. It becomes the highest-average comparator for classification and NER. Existing per-language scores remain unchanged. PIXEL-M4's NER average is corrected from 75.9 to 76.6 in Table 3 and its caption, although Section 4 still states 75.9.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theorems or proofs. The mathematical content underlying pretraining, representation normalization, cosine similarity, and retrieval evaluation is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about multilingual pixel pretraining, non-Latin transfer, linguistic representations, and alignment among pretraining languages. The CANINE-S results do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies unequal pretraining-data exposure as a limitation of the PIXEL-BIGRAMS comparison and explains that a matched-data monolingual control exceeded the compute budget. The underlying unique-data difference was already disclosed in v1 Section 2.1. New CANINE-S discussion also qualifies comparisons by differing pretraining corpora and language coverage.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds CANINE-S implementation guidance by specifying shared experimental settings and hyperparameters. New Appendix A.4 discloses AI assistance for generating plotting code. Existing hyperparameter tables, dataset statistics, and code/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Related Work section are unchanged. Section 3.2 newly positions PIXEL-M4 against CANINE-S, whose underlying work was already cited in v1, explaining differences in representation, pretraining objective, and language exposure.

P1.justification: v2 removes brief section roadmaps, makes localized wording corrections, clarifies PIXEL-BIGRAMS naming in Section 5.3, and adds Appendix A.4. The overall narrative and section order remain intact. Section 2.1 also acquires a duplicated sentence fragment.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 gain CANINE-S rows and revised captions, and Table 1 swaps the BEN/BOD column order. Appendix tables and plots are reflowed, with Tables 5–7 gathered on v2's final page. All figures retain their graphical content and design.

improvement.justification: The CANINE-S comparisons provide useful multilingual context, and the explicit pretraining-data caveats improve interpretive transparency. Correcting Table 3's NER average also improves accuracy. These benefits outweigh limited reporting defects: Section 4 retains the old average, and Table 2's new caption overlooks the displayed Japanese tie. The central data-exposure confound remains uncontrolled.
